newsitem.title: TURKEY: Seventeen dead in Istanbul hotel blaze.
newsitem.headline: Seventeen dead in Istanbul hotel blaze.

text.p: Seventeen people, most believed to be Ukrainian women, died in a fire that broke out at a hotel in central Istanbul early on Sunday, police officials said.

The lower floors of the hotel were gutted by the blaze which started around 4.00 a.m. (0200 GMT) after a gas leak in a shop on the ground floor of the building in Istanbul's Laleli district, television reports said.

They said most of the dead and injured were Ukrainian women, poisoned by smoke inhalation. A police officer told Reuters that 39 people were known to have been hurt in the fire in the seven-storey, three star hotel.
Traders from eastern Europe involved in Istanbul's widespread "suitcase trade" stay in hotels in the crowded Laleli area of the city.
Television pictures showed the injured, their faces blackened by smoke, climbing out of hotel windows and clambering down fire engine ladders.
Fire services quickly brought the blaze under control and the injured were taken to nearby hospitals, the reports said.
Hospital officials said 14 of the dead were women but were unable to confirm their identity or that of the injured. They said some were in a critical condition.
